newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico '97 public investment a 10-yr high - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico '97 public investment a 10-yr high - Zedillo.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo said Thursday that 1997 public investment would be more than 122 billion pesos, almost four percent of GDP and a 10-year high.

"All together, we see the physical investment fostered by the public sector for next year at more than 122 billion pesos...an increase of 25 percent in real terms compared to this year," Zedillo said in a speech to construction industry executives.
The investment figure, he added, "is equivalent to almost four percent of estimated GDP for 1997, the highest percentage in the last 10 years."

Among the areas benefitting from higher spending will be the oil and electricity industries, where investment is set to grow more than 60 percent, and roads and waterworks, where investment is set to rise by about 15 percent, Zedillo said.

Zedillo said public spending in 1997, set in the new economic pact with labour and business leaders announced last Saturday, would "consolidate economic reactivation, give the greatest attention possible to social development programmes and foster investment in infrastructure."
Investment would be carried out both via traditional direct public spending and via schemes where the government tenders projects out to private firms who raise the financing themselves.
